{{Short description|French intellectual, Greek scholar and mathematician}}
[[File:Nicolas de Malezieu - Coste 14372.jpg|thumb|Nicolas de Malezieu |alt=Nicolas de Malezieu - Coste 14372.jpg]]
'''Nicolas de Malézieu''' (or '''Malézieux''')<ref>{{cite book|author=abbé Guillaume Thomas François Raynal|title=Anecdotes littéraires ou histoire de ce qui est arrivé de plus singulier et de plus intéressant aux écrivains françois, depuis le renouvellement des lettres sous François I jusqu'à nos jours|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=B9ETAAAAQAAJ&pg=PA203|year=1752|publisher=Durand|page=203}}</ref> (or '''Malesieu''')<ref>{{cite wikisource |title=Treatise of Human Nature |last= Hume |first= David |authorlink= David Hume |year=1739 |at=1.2.2.3, n. 2 |wslink= Treatise of Human Nature/Book 1: Of the understanding/Part 2/Section 2 |wsat=cite note-2}}</ref> (7 September 1650, in [[Paris]] – 4 March 1727, in Paris) was a French intellectual, [[Ancient Greek literature|Greek scholar]] and [[mathematician]].<ref name="Eloge">{{cite web |title=Éloge de Nicolas de Malézieu par Fontenelle - Histoire de l'Académie royale des sciences - Année 1727 |url=http://www.academie-sciences.fr/pdf/dossiers/Fontenelle/font_pdf/p145_151_vol3589.pdf |website=academie-sciences.fr |publisher=Académie des Sciences |accessdate=15 November 2018}}</ref>

==Life and career==
Nicolas de Malézieu was a [[squire]] and lord of [[Châtenay-Malabry|Chatenay]]. He later became chancellor of [[Dombes]] and secretary-general to the [[Switzerland|Swiss]] and [[Three Leagues|Grisons]] of France. He was the tutor of [[Louis Auguste, Duke of Maine]] (to whom he introduced [[Jacques Bénigne Bossuet|Bossuet]]) and he declaimed the plays of [[Euripides]] and  [[Sophocles]] to the [[Louise Bénédicte de Bourbon|duchess]] who had made her chateau of [[château de Sceaux|Sceaux]] into a literary salon. Here he became a member of the light-hearted fraternity she founded, the (fr) [[:fr:Ordre de la Mouche à Miel|Knights of the Bee]], and organised the festivals she loved, the [[:fr:Grandes Nuits de Sceaux]]. Later tutor to [[Louis, Duke of Burgundy|duc de Bourgogne]], he was appointed to the [[Académie des sciences (France)|Académie royale des sciences]] in 1699 and to the [[Académie française]] in 1701.<ref name="AF">{{cite web |title=Nicolas de MALÉZIEU |url=http://www.academie-francaise.fr/les-immortels/nicolas-de-malezieu |website=academie-francaise.fr |publisher=Académie française |accessdate=15 November 2018}}</ref>

Malézieu collected and published the lessons in mathematics that he gave to the duc de Bourgogne over four years in 1705 as  ''Élémens de géométrie de Mgr le duc de Bourgogne''. Le ''[[Journal des savants]]'' reported in detail the observations he made in this work on geometry and infinitely small numbers. In 1713, this work was translated into Latin as ''Serenissimi Burgundiae Ducis Elementa Geometrica, ex Gallico Semone in Latinum translata ad Usum Seminarii Patavini''. A third (posthumous) edition, with corrections and a supplemental treatise on logarithms, appeared 1729.<ref name="Eloge"/>

Nicolas de Malézieu also translated [[Euripides]]’ ''[[Iphigenia in Tauris]]'' as well as poems, songs and sketches, which were published in 1712 in ''Les Divertissements de Sceaux'' and in 1725 in the ''Suite des Divertissements''. Among these pieces are ''Philémon et Baucis'', ''Le Prince de Cathay'', ''Les Importuns de Chatenay'', ''La Grande Nuit de l'éclipse'', ''L'Hôte de Lemnos'', ''La Tarentole''<ref>{{cite web |title=La Tarentole |url=https://operabaroque.fr/MATHO_TARENTOLE.htm |website=Opera Baroque |accessdate=15 November 2018}}</ref> and ''L'Heautontimorumenos''. Often written in a single day, these pieces were set to music and staged for the amusement of the duchess, to whom Malézieu also gave courses in astronomy.

A four-volume work, a ''Histoire des fermes du roi'' (''History of Royal Farms'') survives only a manuscript version dating from 1746.<ref>Une copie manuscrite de cet ouvrage, datant de 1746, est conservée à Paris au Département des manuscrits de la Bibliothèque nationale de France sous la cote N.A.F. 5010.</ref>

[[Pierre-Édouard Lémontey]] said of Malézieu "Knowing a bit about everything, he gathered in his servile person all the advantages of universal mediocrity."<ref name="AF"/>

==Family==
Malézieu was the son of Nicolas de Malézieu (1612-1652) and Marie des Forges (d.1680).<ref name="Eloge"/> His brother Michel Louis de Malézieu married Marie Jérônime Mac Carthy (d.1714)<ref>{{cite web |title=Nicolas de Malezieu |url=https://gw.geneanet.org/pierfit?lang=fr&n=de+malézieu&oc=0&p=nicolas |website=gw.geneanet.org |publisher=Geneanet |accessdate=15 November 2018}}</ref>

In 1672 Malézieu married Françoise Faudel de Fauveresse (1650-1741) by whom he had the following children:<ref>{{cite book|author=François-Alexandre Aubert de La Chesnaye-Desbois|title=Dictionnaire de la noblesse: contenant les généalogies, l'histoire & la chronologie des familles nobles de France, l'explication de leurs armes & l'état des grandes terres du royaume ... : on a joint à ce dictionnaire le tableau généalogique, historique, des maisons souveraines de l'Europe, & une notice des familles étrangères, les plus anciennes, les plus nobles & les plus illustres ...|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-3hUAAAAYAAJ&pg=PA437|year=1775|publisher=Chez La Veuve Duchesne ... et l'auteur|pages=437–}}</ref>

* Nicolas de Malézieu (1674-1748), bishop of Lavaur en 1713.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bishop Nicolas de Malezieu |url=http://www.catholic-hierarchy.org/bishop/bmalez.html |website=catholic-hierarchy.org |publisher=Catholic Hierarchy |accessdate=15 November 2018}}</ref>
* Pierre de Malézieu (1680-1756), married Louise Marthe Stoppa in 1717 (d.1720), under-secretary to the duc de Maine, secretary-general of the Swiss and Grisons in 1727, brigadier of the infantry, ifnanterie, [[maréchal de camp]] in 1734, lieutenant general of the artillery and commander of the [[Order of Saint-Louis]] in 1756.
* Charles-François de Malézieu (d.1763), lieutenant-colonel of a brigade of [[carabinier]]s, cavalry brigadier in 1745, governor of the harbour and defences of [[La Rochelle]].
* Élisabeth de Malézieu (b.1676), married (1699) Antoine des Rioux de Missimy, first president of the parlement and intendant of Dombes
* Marie de Malézieu (b.1682), married (1705) Louis de Guiry, seigneur de Noncourt and la Roncière, [[mestre de camp]] of the cavalry, lieutenant general of [[Aunis]] and [[la Rochelle]]
